json.summary: A middle-aged man in a waistcoat owns a flatbed truck whose tailgate carries the phone number 7722·683/FELVESZEM, and the truck has been wrecked in an accident. The man speaks to the truck as if it were a stranger, and the truck answers with complaints about its legs, its injuries and the cold, while the man's replies stay crude and exasperated. The joke rests on the deadpan absurdity of a man arguing with his own broken vehicle, which is then treated as a sick patient, and on the crude swearing that is the man's only response. The strip ends with him covering the truck with a blanket, which is a warm, absurd closing beat.

characters.name: truck owner (man in waistcoat)
characters.description: Middle-aged, balding-on-top with a curly side fringe, heavy-lidded and sleepy eyes, a bulbous nose and stubble, wearing a worn waistcoat with pockets over a shirt, and baggy trousers. He is the truck's owner and the main speaker, gruff and exasperated, swearing constantly with 'bazme' (fuck me), 'mi a faszom' (what the fuck), 'akurva élet' (fucking life) and 'geci' (shit). He rarely says anything sincere, and his reactions are mostly incredulous outbursts. In p0 he holds a phone in one hand and is shown as stunned and dazed by the truck's crash.

characters.name: the truck
characters.description: A flatbed lorry with a wooden or metal bed, a tailgate carrying the sign 7722·683/FELVESZEM, and wheels that look broken or sagging. It is the second main voice of the strip: it speaks in dramatic, self-pitying bubbles on the left side of the panels, groaning and complaining about being hit and injured. Its tone is wheezy and melodramatic, as a dying patient would talk.

characters.name: off-panel woman who hit the truck (Gubacs Teréz)
characters.description: Never shown, only named in the truck's speech in r5 as 'Gubacs Teréz'. 'Gubacs' means hunchbacked or gnarled, so the name is a deliberate unflattering nickname. She is the one who hit the truck on the road and caused the damage the truck complains about.

panels.description: The man in the waistcoat stumbles away from the side of the truck with one arm out, clutching a phone in the other hand and looking dazed. The cab window reads 'HLOTT!' in shaky lettering and a small 'RITY!' sits near his phone. The truck's side sign reads 'ÉPÖIPAI KITTELEZÉS • OG', cut off at the panel edge, with a street lamp behind.

The truck's tailgate is seen at left with the sign 7722·683/FELVESZEM, and a groan bubble r1 trails its tail down-left toward the truck. On the right, the man in the waistcoat stands with his hands on his hips and asks 'MI A FASZOM?' (what the fuck), his tail running down to his mouth.

The man stands at the right with his mouth open, addressing r4 ('who are you and what the shit are you doing on my truck bed, bazme?') and his tail runs up to that bubble. The truck at left replies in r5 about being run over by 'Gubacs Teréz' on the road and having both legs broken, and r6 'FEKSZEM ITT' is written across its body as a sign. The tailgate sign reads 7722·683/FELVESZEM.

The man stands at right with one hand resting on the truck's tailgate, and his speech r8 ('I wasn't even on that road today, bazme... not even near it') runs over the top of the panel. The truck's bubble r9 ('Last Tuesday it happened...') sits at left, with its tail pointing back to the truck. The sign on the truck reads 7722·683/FELVESZEM and the man's face is circled as r10, with no text.

The man at right, holding a shopping bag, says r12 ('Last Tuesday? Don't lie to me! Didn't you starve to death?'). The truck at left answers r13 ('I came out of the shop when I got hit full-on... two big bags...'), and its bubble tail points at the truck. The truck's tailgate sign reads 7722·683/FELVESZEM.

The man walks away from the truck at right, face twisted, and says r15 'AKURVA ÉLET!' (fucking life). The truck's tailgate sign reads 7722 · 683/FELVESZEM, and the truck's wheel is shown at the bottom left, with no speech from the truck in this panel.
Only the truck is shown, with a groan r19 'AAAARRRGH....' at top left. The tailgate sign reads 7722 · 683/FELVESZEM.

The man at right gestures at the truck and says r21 ('Here's a blanket, bazme. The nights are already cold.'). Inside the truck bed at left a pillow and blanket are visible, and the tailgate sign reads 7722.683/FELVESZEM. The man's arm and body movements (r23) show him trembling or gesturing with exasperation.

notes: Swearing: 'bazme' is literally 'bazd meg' (fuck you / fuck me), a very common all-purpose curse; the man uses it in r4, r8 and r21 as a tic. 'Mi a faszom' (r2) literally means 'what is my dick', an exasperated 'what the fuck'. 'Akurva élet' (r15) means 'fucking life', with 'akurva' the strongest mild-to-hard curse word in Hungarian. 'Geci' (r4) is a vulgar word for shit.

The truck's speech is in plain colloquial Hungarian with a melodramatic, sick-patient tone, so the translation should keep it sound injured, not witty. 'Fájogat' (r5) is a colloquial variant of 'fáj' (hurts), so keep the stuttering repetition 'FÁJ. FÁJOGAT.' as a whine.

'Gubacs' (r5) means hunchbacked, gnarled or knotty, and is a mildly insulting nickname for the woman who hit the truck. It is not a surname in the usual sense, so translators should keep the nickname visible rather than making it a neutral name.

'Felveszem' (in the 7722·683/FELVESZEM sign, r3, r7, r11, r14, r16, r20, r22) means 'I'll pick it up / I'll answer (the phone)'. The number is a phone number, and the sign on the truck is a sort of call-answering ad. The joke is that the truck is answering calls of its own, so keep the sign as drawn and do not translate it.

Sign running gag: the sign on the tailgate of the truck is the same in every panel (7722·683/FELVESZEM), but the separator changes between a dot, a middle dot and a space, as well as the size of the sign. Treat this as artist drift rather than a deliberate joke, and keep the number exactly as drawn in each panel.

'ÉPÖIPAI KITTELEZÉS • OG' (r0) on the truck side looks like a garbled 'ÉPÍTŐIPARI' (construction trade) plus an unfamiliar word 'KITTELEZÉS', cut off at 'OG'. The spelling is deliberate, so keep it as drawn and do not correct it.

'HLOTT!' on the cab window (not editable) looks like a damaged 'HALOTT' (dead) with the A missing, which is consistent with the truck being on its last legs; keep it as drawn. 'RITY!' next to the man's phone is a sound effect or a fragment of lettering that is not part of the joke.

Running joke of the 'HOGY NEM HALTÁL ÉHEN?' (r12, 'didn't you starve to death?') type: the man treats the truck as a living creature that should have died long ago, so the question is absurd rather than a real question. Translate it as deadpan sarcasm.

The truck speaks in bubbles placed on the left side of the panels (r1, r5, r9, r13, r19), with tails pointing back to the truck. The man speaks on the right (r2, r4, r8, r12, r15, r21). The map of speakers follows these tails, and r6 'FEKSZEM ITT' is typed as a sign but is part of the truck's lament.

'Kiment a boltból' style: 'KÉT NAGY SZATYOR' (r13) means 'two big shopping bags' (szatyor is the classic string or plastic shopping bag). 'TELIBE KAPOTT' is the idiom 'got hit full on', so the truck was hit by something while carrying shopping, which is part of the absurd car-talk-of-bags joke.
Cultural: 'plató' (r2) is the flatbed or truck bed, so 'a platóm' means 'my truck bed'. The man calls the truck his own 'platform', which makes the 'who are you' question more absurd.
